cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities arising from improper handling of user-supplied data during cookie parsing and output generation. Common issues include missing validation of control characters in Set-Cookie headers, unsafe deserialization of cookie data using pickle, prototype pollution from untrusted cookie names, over-broad whitespace trimming causing normalization bypass, and missing output encoding leading to XSS. These flaws allow attackers to inject arbitrary headers, execute arbitrary code, pollute object prototypes, bypass security prefixes, or perform cross-site scripting.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations into outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers. Report code paths where scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets.

mechanism.missing_guard: scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request
mechanism.name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch
mechanism.sink_shape: outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add validation functions to reject or escape characters that can break the HTTP header syntax (e.g., control characters, \r\n, ;) before constructing the Set-Cookie header string.
sub_patterns.name: Missing validation of special characters in Set-Cookie header construction
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes cookie names, values, domains, and paths are safe to embed directly into HTTP Set-Cookie headers without sanitization, allowing injection of control characters (CR, LF) or delimiter characters (semicolon) that can break the header format or inject arbitrary headers.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use null-prototype objects (Object.create(null)) for internal data structures and skip dangerous prototype keys during assignment.
sub_patterns.name: Prototype pollution via cookie name assignment
sub_patterns.root_cause: Cookie parsing uses plain JavaScript objects for the cookie jar and parameters, allowing prototype-related keys like '__proto__' to be set during iteration, polluting Object.prototype.
